fullPassage: Talking about what something smells like is the most basic way of talking about our olfactory experience, and even this most basic way of talking about smells is challenging. There are no words in the English language to describe smells in the same way in which "blue" or "green" describe colors. Instead, to talk about how something smells, we talk about the source of the odor. Things smell "flowery," "fruity," or "fishy." Furthermore, even the most familiar odors are difficult to identify when they are not experienced in their usual context. In one experiment the majority of participants was unable to name very common odors like beer, urine, roses, or motor oil. Obviously, even those who couldn't name any of these odors would drink the beer but not the urine or the motor oil. This is how evolution has shaped our brain: We respond to odors correctly in many different ways, but we are not well-equipped to talk about them.

questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 like의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) like = ~와 같은/처럼(전치사) / (B) like = 좋아하다(동사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) ~와 같은/처럼 — (B) 좋아하다 ←정답
❌ ② (A) 좋아하다 — (B) ~처럼
❌ ③ (A) 원하다 — (B) 비슷한
❌ ④ (A) ~처럼 — (B) 원하다

(A) 'what it smelled like(그것이 어떤 냄새가 났는지)'에서 like는 '~와 같은/처럼'을 뜻하는 전치사예요.

(B) 'children like the sweet smell(아이들이 향을 좋아한다)'에서 like는 '좋아하다'라는 동사예요.

따라서 (A) ~처럼 — (B) 좋아하다 조합인 ①번이 정답이에요. ←정답
det.tip: like: 전치사 '~처럼' vs 동사 '좋아하다' — 문맥으로 구분

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a scientific test that is done in order to discover something or to prove that an idea is true"

det.korean: 정의 = '무언가를 발견하거나 어떤 생각이 참임을 증명하기 위해 하는 과학적 시험' → experiment(실험)
det.analysis:
❌① mistake(실수): 의도된 시험이 아니라 어긋나요.

❌② tradition(전통): 과학적 시험과 무관해요.

✅③ experiment(실험): '무언가를 알아내기 위한 과학적 시험'이라는 정의와 정확히 일치해요. 지문의 experiment와 같아요. ←정답

❌④ accident(사고): 계획된 시험이 아니라 어긋나요.

questions.passage: Obviously, even those who couldn't name any of these odors would drink the beer but not the urine or the motor oil. This is how evolution has __________ (shape) our brain: We respond to odors correctly in many different ways, but we are not well-equipped to talk about them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: shape(동사, 형성하다) → shaped(과거분사). 'has + 과거분사'인 현재완료 자리예요.
det.analysis: 빈칸은 'evolution has __________'으로, 'has + 과거분사(p.p.)' 현재완료 형태가 필요해요. 동사 shape(형성하다)를 과거분사 shaped로 바꿔야 '진화가 뇌를 형성해 왔다'가 돼요.

questions.passage: Furthermore, even the most familiar odors are difficult to identify when they are not __________ (experience) in their usual context. In one experiment the majority of participants was unable to name very common odors like beer, urine, roses, or motor oil.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: experience(동사, 경험하다) → experienced(과거분사). 'are not + 과거분사'인 수동태 자리예요.
det.analysis: 빈칸은 'when they are not __________ in their usual context'로, 'be동사 + 과거분사'인 수동태 자리예요. 냄새가 평소 맥락에서 '경험되지' 않을 때라는 수동 의미라 동사 experience를 과거분사 experienced로 바꿔야 해요.

questions.passage: Talking about what something smells like is the most basic way of talking about our olfactory experience, and even this most basic way of talking about smells is challenging. There are no words in the English language to describe smells in the same way in which "blue" or "green" describe colors. Instead, to talk about how something smells, we talk about __________. Things smell "flowery," "fruity," or "fishy." Furthermore, even the most familiar odors are difficult to identify when they are not experienced in their usual context. In one experiment the majority of participants was unable to name very common odors like beer, urine, roses, or motor oil. Obviously, even those who couldn't name any of these odors would drink the beer but not the urine or the motor oil. This is how evolution has shaped our brain: We respond to odors correctly in many different ways, but we are not well-equipped to talk about them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: the source of the odor — 냄새 자체 대신 냄새의 '원천'을 언급하며 이야기한다.
det.analysis:
✅① the source of the odor(냄새의 원천): '꽃 향', '생선 냄새'처럼 냄새의 출처(원천)에 빗대어 말한다는 흐름과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌② the color of the object(대상의 색): 냄새를 색으로 표현한다는 것은 어색해요.

❌③ the price of the item(물건의 가격): 문맥과 무관해요.

❌④ the name of the person(사람의 이름): 문맥과 안 맞아요.

questions.passage: Talking about what something smells like is the most basic way of talking about our olfactory experience, and even this most basic way of talking about smells is challenging. There are no words in the English language to describe smells in the same way in which "blue" or "green" describe colors. Instead, to talk about how something smells, we talk about the source of the odor. Things smell "flowery," "fruity," or "fishy." Furthermore, even the most familiar odors are difficult to identify when they are not experienced in their usual context. In one experiment the majority of participants was unable to name very common odors like beer, urine, roses, or motor oil. Obviously, even those who couldn't name any of these odors would drink the beer but not the urine or the motor oil. This is how evolution has shaped our brain: We respond to odors correctly in many different ways, but we are __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: not well-equipped to talk about them — 냄새에는 잘 반응하지만, 그것을 말로 표현하는 데에는 '잘 갖춰져 있지 않다'.
det.analysis:
❌① perfectly able to describe them(완벽히 묘사할 수 있다): 글 전체 주장(말로 표현하기 어렵다)과 정반대예요.

✅② not well-equipped to talk about them(그것을 말로 표현하는 데 서투르다): '냄새에는 올바르게 반응하지만'과 대조를 이루는 결론이라 맞아요. ←정답

❌③ unable to react to them at all(전혀 반응하지 못한다): 앞의 '올바르게 반응한다'와 모순돼요.

❌④ born without any sense of smell(후각 없이 태어난다): 본문에 없는 내용이에요.
det.tip: respond correctly ↔ but not well-equipped to talk (대조)
